source.title: Wisdom is Knowing What not to Say: Hallucination-Free LLMs Unlearning via Attention Shifting
source.authors: Chen-Chen Tan; You-Yang Qu; Xing-Hao Li; Hui Zhang; Shu-Jie Cui; Cun-Jian Chen; Long-Xiang Gao

page_placements.theme: Forgotten knowledge re-emerges through later non-adversarial updates

record.file_problem: None noted; full paper and supplemental material are present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether prompt variants recover target information after its own attention-shifting unlearning method, using behavioral metrics rather than the original methods or measures in the claim.
record.gate_note: The paper reports no fine-tuning, activation-direction ablation, or quantization recovery experiment. Its reported prompt-variant results are included; cited findings from other work are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: Proposes a new unlearning method, Attention Shifting (AS). It tests whether rephrased, perturbed or noised queries recover the forgotten ToFU facts (Table 4), which bears on E and on F's robustness claim. It also reports forgetting and retention results relevant to A. It runs no fine-tuning, ablation or quantization attack.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct, but it leaves out the headline. The authors conclude that AS gives hallucination-free behavioural unlearning: 0% GPT-4-judged reproduction and hallucination, high top-k exclusion, and preserved or improved neighbouring and general accuracy (up to 15% higher than baselines on ToFU and 10% on TDEC). They also say it holds against the prompt variants they tested. They concede it is suppression rather than erasure. They also state, without testing it, that fine-tuning on unlearned data can reintroduce the knowledge and that probing might expose latent traces.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces attention-weight suppression and retention adapters with a dual-loss objective; it does not reproduce the cited gradient-ascent, Who’s Harry Potter, or RMU methods.
record.method_sensitivity: Prompt variant changes ROUGE-L from 0.02 on original-form queries to 0.07–0.11 on perturbed, noised, and rephrased queries; TR@50 remains 0.92–0.94.

fits_no_version.finding: Logit-level baselines (IHL, ULD) leave unlearned tokens in the top-5 predictions much more often than AS or GA (TR 0.45-0.62 against 0.97-0.98, Table 1). The authors read this as such methods leaving knowledge partially accessible.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Logit-suppression unlearning leaves target tokens in the top-k predictions, a sign of shallow forgetting.

fits_no_version.finding: Under rephrased, perturbed and noised queries, AS's GPT-4-judged hallucination rate rises from 0.00 to 0.05-0.07 (Table 4, HR). HR counts fabricated wrong answers, not recovery of the forgotten facts.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal-style unlearning drifts toward fabricated answers when queries are rephrased.

fits_no_version.finding: Adding retain-set CE or KL losses during unlearning raises target ROUGE-L for the baselines (GA 0.08 to 0.15/0.20; NPO 0.14 to 0.16/0.26; IHL 0.25 to 0.52/0.47; Table 1). The authors read this as retention losses reactivating suppressed knowledge.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Retain-set regularization during unlearning partly reactivates the forgotten knowledge.

record.peer_reviewed: Preprint; text says under review. Venue is listed as Neural Information Processing Systems.
record.problems: Prompt-variant evidence is reported for ToFU and one stated target model; no uncertainty is reported for Table 4. Reproduction and hallucination measures elsewhere use GPT-4 as an automated evaluator. The paper does not test the fine-tuning, internal-edit, or quantization recovery attacks. Its internal-trace statements are limitations/possibilities, not recovery experiments.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant prompt-variant rows omitted. Other benchmark and utility results not included where they do not measure recovery or the specific parts of the listed claim versions.

untested.parts: No chance-level or never-trained comparison. Robustness is tested only against prompt variants, not fine-tuning, ablation or quantization.
Entirely untested. The limitations say fine-tuning on unlearned data can reintroduce the knowledge, but no experiment is reported.

Entirely untested. There is no ablation or probing. The base weights are frozen and only adapters are trained, so the knowledge stays in the base weights by design. The authors concede 'behavioural suppression rather than complete representational erasure', but no experiment tests access.

Jailbreaks, other languages and in-context information are untested. Only rephrased, perturbed and noised queries are tested, on ToFU with Llama-2-7B, and the paper does not describe how the variants were built.
Resistance to fine-tuning, internal edits and quantization is untested. Prompt variants are tested only on ToFU with one model.

missing.what: TUD-Var (rephrased/noised TUD) results across AS hyperparameters. In the λ sweep, the ΔROUGE-L columns go from about -64%/-69% at λ=0.2 to about -98%/-99% at λ=0.99 (column order unclear in the flattened text). The α sweep gives TUD-Var 0.05-0.09 (0.06 for dynamic α). Recovery under prompt variants depends on suppression strength.
The same Table 7 TUD-Var results, read as the counter-method's resistance to prompt variants depending on λ and α (HR also falls from 0.62 at λ=0.2 to 0.00 at λ=0.99)
AS forgetting on Forget-01/Forget-10: TUD ROUGE-L 0.05/0.01, TR@5 0.98/0.99, NEK accuracy 0.79 (+0.09)/0.73 (+0.03), GEK accuracy 0.84 (+0.01)/0.79 (-0.04)
GPT-4-judged reproduction rate of 0% (hallucination 0%) for AS, against higher rates for the baselines
LLaMA-13B on PubMedQA: target ΔROUGE-L -93 to -98%, TR@50 0.90-0.96, remaining ΔROUGE-L between -0.2 and +1.3
Baseline methods' TUD ROUGE-L, TR and retention (GA, NPO, IHL, ULD). GA and NPO forget but lose 0.35-0.58 of NEK/GEK accuracy.

TDEC on GPT-Neo 125M/1.3B/2.7B: at a fixed el10 ≤ 0.05 forgetting threshold, AS keeps the highest neighbouring accuracy and model utility; utility is also tracked over sequential unlearning requests (figures only)

record.verdict_notes:
Changes from the earlier verdict:
(1) Merged the duplicate row_fixes items for r11-r16 (the validator flagged only r12, r14 and r16, but r11, r13 and r15 were duplicated too) into one item per row with versions [E, F]. States follow the recovery effect each row measures: r11, r13 and r15 partial; r12, r14 and r16 absent. The problem text says that for F an absent recovery means resistance held.
(2) Removed F from r1 and r2: Table 1 has no attack, so these rows measure forgetting, not resistance.
(3) Took the hallucination rate out of the F limits_scope reason and moved it from missing to fits_no_version, because HR counts fabricated wrong answers, not recovery.
(4) Split missing[].versions into single declared ids. Refined the Table 7 entry (λ dependence) and added a TDEC entry for A.
(5) Added a fits_no_version finding on retain losses reactivating knowledge. Corrected GA's TR to 0.98 in the existing entry.
(6) Noted under untested C that the base weights are frozen.
(7) Expanded authors_conclusion.

Kept the earlier verdict's relation, tranche, labels and other row states.

Other notes: Table 4's original-query ROUGE-L (0.02) differs from Table 1's (0.16) without explanation. TR uses k=5 in Table 1 and k=50 in Table 4. Table 4 gives no uncertainty and does not say how the variants were generated. Hallucination and reproduction rates rely on a GPT-4 judge. The authors' remarks on fine-tuning relearning, latent traces, and sequential requests being 'partially reversed' by similar retain data are assertions, not evidence for B or C. The text contained no instructions to the reader.

versions.untested_parts: The paper reports unlearning and retention results, but does not compare targeted accuracy with chance. It tests prompt variants, not fine-tuning, activation ablation, or quantization attacks.
No small-set recovery experiment. The limitations mention fine-tuning on unlearned data, but report no experiment testing it.

No activation-direction ablation is performed. The paper discusses behavioral suppression versus complete representational erasure and possible latent traces, but does not experimentally test recovery through internal edits or probing.
Tests rephrased, perturbed, and noised queries. Does not test jailbreaks, other languages, or in-context information.
Tests the proposed method against prompt variants only; does not test resistance to fine-tuning, activation edits, or quantization.
